topic: Bookmaker odds-movement algorithms, overround de-vigging and exchange market making
scope: Open-source GitHub repositories and peer-reviewed economics/microstructure papers on bookmaker pricing, favourite-longshot bias, dynamic odds adjustment, and betting-exchange liquidity provision.
verification_summary: Commercial sportsbook cores remain proprietary. Repositories below were verified via README/API metadata and algebraic cross-checking against peer-reviewed papers; none establishes a guaranteed live Betfair profit.

repositories.verified_code_vs_readme: Equations for Shin (Jullien-Salanie), Balanced Books (Fingleton-Waldron), Power (Clarke et al.), Odds Ratio (Cheung) and Additive/WPO independently verified algebraically in betangel_research/bookmaker_pricing.py.
what_it_gets_right: Separates profit-maximizing Shin from risk-minimizing Balanced Books and empirical Power/Odds-Ratio curves.
what_it_gets_wrong_or_misses: Static odds snapshot conversion only; does not model two-sided exchange ladders, cross-matching, or queue execution.
repositories.limitations: Converts static fixed-odds vectors to probabilities; no order-book microstructure or live execution model.

repositories.verified_code_vs_readme: Documented Python implied submodule implements Shin, Power, Odds Ratio, Additive and Multiplicative methods.
what_it_gets_right: Clean Python API returning solved method parameters (z, k) alongside implied probabilities.
what_it_gets_wrong_or_misses: Oriented around football outcome models rather than multi-runner horse-racing exchange ladders.
repositories.limitations: Football-first library; does not handle Betfair CLASSIC ticks, cross-matching, or pre-off horse-racing streams.

repositories.verified_code_vs_readme: Returns implied probabilities, insider fraction z, iterations and convergence delta; handles n=2 cleanly.
what_it_gets_right: Exposes insider-trading share z and solver convergence diagnostics.
what_it_gets_wrong_or_misses: Requires non-negative overround and cannot de-vig underround Betfair lay books.

repositories.verified_code_vs_readme: Replication package for Kaunitz, Zhong & Kreiner documenting both mathematical soft-book mispricing and live account limiting.
what_it_gets_right: Proves with live bets that retail bookmakers protect margins by gubbing/capping sharps rather than solely moving odds.
what_it_gets_wrong_or_misses: Football fixed-odds focus; does not generalize to peer-to-peer betting exchanges where accounts are not gubbed.
repositories.limitations: Live phase confirmed practical unviability on retail sportsbooks due to account restrictions and resulting sampling bias.

repositories.verified_code_vs_readme: Documents binary Avellaneda-Stoikov reservation price, EWMA volatility, time-to-expiry tau and inventory skew.
what_it_gets_right: Adapts inventory skew and spread width explicitly to binary expiry risk and time remaining.
what_it_gets_wrong_or_misses: Built for 1-99c binary markets (Kalshi/Polymarket), not Betfair CLASSIC non-uniform ticks or multi-runner cross-matching.
repositories.limitations: Open-source reference strategy without independently audited long-term live profit records.

repositories.verified_code_vs_readme: Paradigm Automated Research Hackathon (April 2026) #2 entry separating latency arbitrageurs from retail flow.
what_it_gets_right: Models the exact adverse-selection tension between toxic fast takers and uninformed retail takers.
what_it_gets_wrong_or_misses: Evaluated in a synthetic 1-99c hackathon simulator rather than real Betfair exchange queues.
repositories.limitations: Hackathon simulation performance does not establish live betting-exchange profitability.

academic_references.citation: Shin, H. S. (1992, 1993) & Jullien, B., & Salanie, B. (1994). Measuring the incidence of insider trading in betting markets. Economic Journal.
academic_references.mechanism: Profit-maximizing bookmaker compresses longshot odds nonlinearly against insider share z.
academic_references.limitations: Assumes representative risk-neutral bookmaker and non-negative overround.

academic_references.citation: Levitt, S. D. (2004). Why are gambling markets organised so differently from financial markets? Economic Journal, 114(495), 223-246.
academic_references.mechanism: Demonstrates bookmakers hold directional exposure and shade prices against predictable bettor biases rather than simply balancing books.
academic_references.limitations: Empirical sample is an NFL betting tournament, not UK horse racing.

academic_references.citation: Whelan, K. (2024, 2025/2026). Risk aversion and FLB (Economica); Agreeing to disagree: The economics of betting exchanges (UCD WP25/22).
academic_references.mechanism: Derives FLB from risk aversion + belief disagreement without insiders; finds Betfair soccer makers ~break-even due to adverse fill selection.
academic_references.limitations: Exchange empirical dataset covers soccer (2022-24), not UK/IE horse racing.

proposed_hypotheses.question: Do FLB-aware de-vigging models (Shin, Power, Odds Ratio) on pre-off Betfair books reduce race-level log loss vs multiplicative normalization?
proposed_hypotheses.falsification: No paired race-level log-loss improvement on untouched chronological folds.

proposed_hypotheses.question: Does rejecting passive LP quotes with XM phantom spreads, elevated Shin z, or quotes inside the Glosten-Milgrom bound reduce +60 s and BSP adverse mark-outs?
proposed_hypotheses.falsification: Filtered fills show no adverse mark-out reduction or non-positive net realised spread.
